title: Pointer Events API: unified mouse, pen, and touch input
learningObjectives: Explain pointer events api: unified mouse, pen, and touch input and the problem it addresses.
Use the relevant language or browser API with valid syntax.
Compare the technique with modern alternatives and identify when each is appropriate.
Handle errors, boundaries, security, and compatibility deliberately.
Test the implementation and explain its behaviour with evidence.

understand.concept: The Pointer Events API provides a unified event model for mouse, pen, and touch input. Core events include pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, pointercancel, pointerover, pointerout, and pointerenter/leave. PointerEvent exposes pointerId, pointerType, isPrimary, pressure, and coordinates. setPointerCapture can keep subsequent pointer events directed to an element after the pointer moves outside it. Use touch-action to declare which gestures the browser may handle, and handle pointercancel because the browser can interrupt a gesture. Do not assume one pointer or a mouse-only device.
understand.whyItMatters: Modern interfaces must support touch screens, styluses, trackpads, and mouse input. Pointer Events reduce duplicated input code while preserving device-specific information when needed.
understand.analogy: Pointer Events provide one common control panel for several kinds of pointing devices.
understand.analogyLimit: The shared event model does not make all devices identical; pressure, hover, multitouch, and gesture behaviour vary.

explain.narrative: Create a draggable item using pointerdown, pointermove, pointerup, and pointercancel. Capture the pointer after the drag begins and release it when the interaction ends.

examples.explanation: The element captures the active pointer so it continues receiving events when the pointer leaves its bounds. A real implementation must also handle lostpointercapture and cleanup.
examples.expectedOutput: The console logs the device type and pointer ID when a pointer interaction starts.

examples.explanation: The touch-action property tells the browser which gestures it may handle. pan-y allows vertical browser panning while the application can implement an appropriate horizontal gesture.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser retains vertical scrolling while the app can handle a horizontal drag gesture.

practise.guidedTask: Build a pointer-aware drawing or drag interaction. Support mouse, touch, and pen; handle pointercancel; and test more than one pointer where the design allows it.
practise.independentTask: Implement a robust gesture component with pointer capture, touch-action, cancellation, cleanup, keyboard alternatives, and tests for multi-touch and device changes.
hints: Use pointerId to track the active pointer rather than assuming only one exists.
Handle pointercancel and lostpointercapture as well as pointerup.
Set touch-action deliberately so browser scrolling and app gestures do not conflict.
